utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I apologise for the delay, because I did not think there was some technical problems. Anyway, this is a Status Conference, the subject is to do with 65 ter filings by the Defence counsel of Mr. Blagojevic. We appreciate the effort made by Defence counsel to submit new 65 ter filings; however, as I mentioned before we are not quite satisfied with this new filing because we see very few improvements compared with the last one. Are there any changes or suggestions for changes by the Defence counsel at this moment? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. I should note that my last filing was almost contemporaneous to the Court's initial remarks, and hence there were not significant changes. However, we take to heart the Court's concerns and we certainly want to make the Court satisfied. So just to bring everybody up-to-date, and I can be corrected by my colleagues if I misspeak. But after the opening statement, the parties met, my recollection was two plus hours. It could have been less. It seemed to me like three hours, but I would say at least two hours where I was asked numerous questions regarding specific individuals on the list, and I was providing them with a verbal supplementation on any particular witness that they had in mind. I also noted at that time that certain decisions had been made with respect to shifting some of the viva voce to 92 bis. I also indicated that there was one witness who was initially scheduled for 92 who was being shifted to viva voce. Now, there is a reason for that, and the reason for that is because this individual was the head of the rocket platoon, and I must say that having looked at the Court's findings in the 98 bis ruling that some significance had been placed on members of the Bratunac Brigade firing rockets --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears Mr. Karnavas is using this situation to be able to argue his case and argue his witnesses. This is -- I have restrained from trying to argue my case or respond, but this whole problem with him providing 65 ter and proofing notes is allowing him to get up and argue his case. It just -- it's unnecessary. And now he's responding to your Rule 98 motion, which I would love to respond to your Rule 98 motion, but I don't think it's really the place or the time to do it. This is happening with each one of his witnesses. He gets a little chat about the witnesses before they testify. And you don't want to hear from me about each of his witnesses after his chat. So I would ask him to try to restrain himself with his argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may just briefly respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I have been in the trial long enough to know that there is going to be a question from you as to why this person is being shifted from 92 to viva voce.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So anticipating the question you're going to ask me, I thought I would take the initiative to answer the question, and I can't do it unless I put it into context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you tell me the number of this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- in your 65 ter filings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's number 38. It's not quite clear yet because of the -- this particular witness, as I understand, has some health problems at the time, at the moment. But in light of our concerns and having -- again and I don't want to argue my case and I won't. But as you might recall the timing of it, the decision came out on the 98 bis just about when we were preparing our supplemental 65 ter, and we already had filed one. And so obviously I think it would be malpractice if I didn't look into the Court's reasoning and try to make some adjustments so that in the final decision you would have all the information available to make the final decisions. So hence that's why with this particular individual it would appear that we might be shifting - I underscore might be shifting - from 92 to viva voce. And I explained this. Mr. McCloskey wasn't there when I explained to his colleagues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you want to hear our comments on this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you want to hear our comments on this witness at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't -- I would suspect that -- and again, I wouldn't want to presume, knowing what the Court has in mind or in its mind, but I would suspect that based on the limited nature of the information in the 65 ter pleading that the Court is concerned that this witness, at least at this time, with this information, should not come viva voce. And I would assume that the Court is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, not only that -- well, judging from the contents in the 65 ter filings, we even don't think it's necessary for him to be a 92 bis witness, because we need the additional information. There is no details in the 65 ter filings. So based, I must say, based on your filings we have serious doubts whether we should have it at all or not. This is our concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand all of this, Your Honour. And I don't -- again, if I am repeating myself, I apologise. But we were not given a sufficient amount of time to supplement this particular filing in light of the timing when the decision came out, when we had to present -- start presenting our case, and all the other logistics that are involved. And so it's not that I am -- and as you might note, co-counsel in this case is in the field meeting with other witnesses, taking other 92 bis statements. And so if I were given some additional time and pointed -- and if the Trial Chamber wished with these additional numbers. If the Trial Chamber pointed out which particular witnesses it wished for me to supplement, I could do that, especially in light of the fact that next Friday we have off. And I can have it over the following weekend. And frankly, it's a Herculean task with witnesses coming in, me prepping them, writing the proofing notes so that the Prosecution won't be complaining. So I just don't have the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you have enough time. We have an extra long break after the Prosecution's case. And before we come to the specific witnesses, would you tell us some good news, that is you changed some live witnesses into the 92 bis witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You want the actual names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. I just want the numbers because we don't know the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, the numbers themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay -- and again, this is tentative. One would be number 43 -- there are several that come under the category of Bratunac Brigade military police. We are significantly reducing that number -- well, maybe not significantly. I'll just stick with reducing. I don't want to -- I believe number 45 is another witness. There is number 21. There is 20. So 20 and 21. I believe, I believe, number 23 as well. And again, I apologise for not being quite as assertive, because I don't like to make these decisions -- I mean, the decisions have been made but everything is shifting at this point. We're still trying to figure out logistically how we can accommodate the time period yet put our case, and of course, make sure that things don't get lost in the 92 bis land, which I must say I don't feel comfortable with this particular procedure. I know it exists, but I don't feel comfortable with it. So to me, I would like to have as few 92 bis as possible and as many viva voce. I'm just being honest, but I'm being realistic as well, knowing that the decisions rest with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's come to the specific witnesses in that list. I would like to share our views with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's come to the witness number 9. I believe that you mentioned about this witness before concerning with the mobilisation of the private bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Do you think that witness is necessary because from -- again, I have to say that based on your filings we didn't see any relevance to this case. Don't you think that the private buses or some other transportation means owned by other units were used for that transportation, there is no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So what's the purpose on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The purpose, Your Honour, is that first of all we went -- okay. We started from the general and now we're going to the specific. We started with, for instance, how the process works for mobilisation and then -- now you have a particular individual who was -- who had a bus and his bus was actually mobilised. So now we have a concrete example of that process. That's number one. Number two, because it was his bus, he was given the opportunity to drive the bus. Again, we see the rules in practice. Number three, this particular individual was a member of the Bratunac Brigade at the time. And because he was given -- his bus was being mobilised and was given the opportunity to drive that bus, without getting any authorisation from anyone, drove the bus. Because it was his private property. And while -- and this individual ended up going to Potocari, he will describe what he saw and what he did, including, including, at one point in time where he was assisting certain individuals get on the bus and taking them to safety, all of which, all of which, in my opinion, defy or contradict parts of the Prosecution case that members of the Bratunac Brigade were there in Potocari committing heinous crimes. So I think this is a concrete example. I thought it would be necessary for us to see the actual rules in practice. And again you have a member of the Bratunac Brigade who is there and we're trying to explain how he got there and what he's doing. Because the Prosecution's case has been that there were members there and is placing a certain significance. So we're trying to show that some, yes, were there and what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And should we come to private session? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again counsel is arguing the case for the Prosecution, suggesting my case is this and my case is that. He's flat out wrong and he's misstating the facts. And I know you're trying to get something to base your decisions on here, but it's appropriate to do it in a different fashion than this because I would prefer not to stand up at all in this hearing, if I can help it. There are certain things that aren't even contested that he's saying are contested and that is not helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we just want to get a rough idea of the contents of this witness's testimony, which should be included in the 65 ter filings. But since we don't have any latest supplementary filings, so we have to make the best use of that. But, Mr. Karnavas, would you please try to avoid any direct mentioning of the Prosecution's case. Just tell us the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Well, directly, no, but indirectly I have to in order to show you how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that. Let's come to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Karnavas, I will draw your attention to witness number 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Number 27 is the commander of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's up there by the Zvornik area. And there have been some -- it's tough for me not to argue against their case or what I believe their case is. And I think it's necessary to hear from this individual as to what his orders were subsequent to the fall of Srebrenica, because we see that the column leaves and is heading in that direction, what his engagement was. We know that there was an order to search the terrain, but with respect to the 4th Battalion that order was slightly different. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes. The problem on our side is that if we are going to hear this witness, including the witness number 26, we need more information about their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because from your 65 filings, it leads up to nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was just being very general, Your Honour. But if you tell me which numbers, and I will provide those -- that additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Number 26, 27 we need more detailed information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And as for witness 25 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's being switched over, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. I haven't been informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I hadn't got to that yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. And number 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Number 19?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Number 19?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought I had just indicated, Your Honour, that he would be coming next week. And briefly if I could just -- since he's coming, I can give you an update.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is he the legal officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, number 19 is the individual who -- this is -- number 19 is the individual that was there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think we have some problems with the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm looking at the latest -- I didn't mean to confuse the Trial Chamber, but when I filed my -- when I filed the April 7 pleading, the amended one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So we could work off of one set of numbers as opposed to referring to the first and the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the person who is a legal officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The legal officer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We just don't know the relevancy of his testimony to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the relevancy of his case is -- I believe there's been some testimony presented by the Prosecution with respect to his activities on July 12th or July 13th. He was also -- his office was right where the military police are situated of the Bratunac Brigade. And so this gentleman is going to be testifying with respect to what orders he had received, particularly received an order from Colonel Beara. He's going to be talking about questioning certain individuals that were brought there to him to be questioned. And he's also going to be talking about -- he's also going to be talking about having a walk with Colonel Beara on the night of the 13th, where he just walked into town with him. And also, in light of his position as a lawyer and later on subsequent and working on a commission for the return of abandoned property, he is going to be providing us with an analysis of the law on that commission that was set up, demonstrating that laws were in place, that abandoned property was not permanently abandoned, but rather there was a process for refugees to temporarily move in, hence the argument that because of the civil war there was anticipation by virtue of the legislation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That issue relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's relevant to the ethnic cleansing argument, Your Honour, that the attack on Srebrenica was for purely ethnic cleansing purposes. I think it's vital to at least know that there was a process in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, that's not the Prosecution's argument, just to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know what their argument is, but I don't want to be facing closing argument and not have laid the foundation to demonstrate that there was a process in place, that simply because somebody left his home that they were not entitled to get that home back. And if a legislation existed prior to the attack on Srebrenica, it clearly demonstrates that by the people that were engaged in these activities on both sides, that it was understood that at some point they would have the legal right to move back in. And I think there is some precedent, I believe coming out of the -- trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And how about witness number 32? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he's got different numbers. I think we have different numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, really? I think this is the April 8th --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: April 8th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, April 7th filings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I can -- this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We need more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I can provide more information. I can give a verbal right now, if you wish, or I can provide more information later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to all this verbal stuff. His chance to get the facts and the issues is better argued written. It's a record for you. This is a shot, but getting it verbally is impossible to respond to. It's not really helpful to keep track of -- there's too many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to be helpful, Your Honour. That's what I'm trying to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let us first of all identify those witnesses that we are not satisfied with your filings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Number 34. Number 41. I believe this witness is essentially looking to impeach the testimony of Mr. Nikolic, which seems unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he needs to clear his name. He's been accused of killing six people; the Prosecution is arguing that. They brought in their witness, Momir Nikolic, to say that. As you might recall, I had urged the Prosecutor at the time to bring this individual in. I wasn't allowed. I had also suggested that I might be present at Momir Nikolic's sentencing so that I could at least question this individual when he was being questioned. And as I understand he wasn't questioned -- or he was questioned rather severely and cross-examined, and his character for truthfulness was put into jeopardy as a result of that vigorous cross-examination. I think I'm entitled to have my record with respect to those six individuals that Momir Nikolic claims this individual killed, because obviously he's a deputy commander or deputy chief of the military police, which falls directly under the commander's responsibility in a sense. And so -- and you know, of course I also want to establish the motive. We have clear motive for Momir Nikolic. I am not through prosecuting Momir Nikolic for his credibility. And again I think this needs to come in. I don't think the gentleman was given a fair opportunity in my opinion to present his full picture as to how it fits into our case when he testified the last time. He was questioned, but he wasn't questioned by us. So we do have a right to bring this witness in in order to establish especially the motive, because again I want to have -- I want to show the clear motive, the mind, the mind of the -- perjurious mind of Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "The perjurious mind of Momir Nikolic." This -- we might be able to work out some sort of stipulation that this person would deny that he killed these six people. I have no -- I mean, I don't know why we need to bring him up if we can also mention the fact that he also corroborates the critical story of going up and down the road calling Muslims down from the woods. So we might be able to solve that. He did give a police report to the MUP where I think he basically states that, and we may be able to agree that that comes in under some form of 92 bis. But this allegation of six people, that's something we can agree with. I don't think that's a big problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the Prosecutor is conceding that Momir Nikolic lied, a false testimony under oath, about those six individuals, that Mr. Petrovic allegedly killed, then that would satisfy me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's something to be discussed between the parties after court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The next witness is witness 42, which we found that his testimony overlaps with the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll provide more information on number 42, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And as for the witness number 41, the parties argued a lot. I hope you could solve this problem out of Court, and I believe that he gave the testimony in the Milosevic case. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He gave testimony, Your Honour, in the Momir Nikolic's sentencing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we admit his statement as 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish I could. This is why I was trying to -- I don't mean to be disputatious, but I think not all the questions for the defence were asked. He was viciously cross-examined, not by one of the Defence lawyers, but both of them. Both of Mr. Nikolic's Defence lawyers took a shot at the gentleman. Now, I will -- in light of the Court's concerns, I will give it some enormous consideration to see if I can provide with a 92 bis statement that would supplement his testimony, which I would also be asking to come in. And I think that's -- I think I'm offering some sort of a middle ground here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you could discuss it with the Prosecution after Court. And as for the witness 45 and 46, we found the testimony of those two witnesses are redundant. Can you consider putting one into 92 bis at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 45 I believe, Your Honour, will be 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. And witness 59 and 60, we believe those two witness's testimony are redundant in light of the witness 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Your Honour. Okay -- well, Your Honour, if I might say one word on this. Any witness -- any name that is mentioned by the Prosecutor in the indictment and any member of the Bratunac Brigade that might be -- might have been identified by the Prosecution in the video footage, I believe it would -- it's my intention, my intention, to bring them in -- at least that's what I would like to. Because I think the Prosecution has made a large argument, a significant argument, as to what they were doing, why they were there, and so on and so forth. And I think bringing some of them in and not all of them may not be sufficient. I don't want there to be any doubt in the Trial Chamber's mind. In other words, I'm going beyond a reasonable doubt. I want to go beyond any doubt that those individuals were not doing anything improper. And that's why I want to give the Trial Chamber an opportunity to see them and to hear their testimony and to give the Prosecutor every opportunity to question them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to avoid the cumulative testimony of those witnesses, if they are testifying about the same thing. You know, there's other channels that we could use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. Today we had a witness that testified somewhat similar to the previous gentleman. The previous gentleman's credibility was attacked, as it should be under cross-examination. By bringing in a second witness from a different angle, a different point of view in my opinion gives the Trial Chamber a better understanding as to whether one or both are telling an accurate picture, what portions to believe or disbelieve. So that is the purpose of doing this, not to accumulate or to drag this trial out longer than it should.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to let the Court and Mr. Karnavas know, the Prosecution is certainly open to Rule 92 bis for these sorts of witnesses. And though I haven't seen a 92 bis statement yet, that will be the tell of all. And unlike what Mr. Karnavas is suggesting, while there are many, many Bratunac Brigade soldiers in Potocari - I think the video speaks for itself - most of them are not directly committing crimes. There are people that are putting people on buses. We're not suggesting, for example, this person that was just mentioned, who I think is sitting on a tank, is committing some crime. If there's a simple 92 bis statement where he wants to come in and say: "I was in Potocari. I saw nothing. I did nothing. Nothing happened," I mean, that's something we can live with because that's a repetitive theme of these witnesses which in some cases I don't even need to cross-examine. But we're not slandering these individual privates that are down there in Potocari. As you know, the theme of this case is there are large numbers of soldiers and commanders from the Bratunac Brigade there with their eyes open and their ears open. And the Bratunac Brigade is close by. But this is not -- these aren't attempts to say that these soldiers are actually committing crimes. I'm not going to say that unless I have evidence. And as this Court knows, when I have evidence, you have seen it generally already. So I am open to reasonable 92 bis denials of see, hear -- hear no evil, speak no evil, see no evil. But a whole series of soldiers coming up and saying that is truly a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope Mr. Karnavas could take into consideration the suggestions from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I dare say with the greatest respect, with the greatest respect, I cannot. I heard two words that cause me some anxiety: "Directly" and "actually." They weren't directly committing crimes so that leaves the possibility for indirectly committing crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We're not going into the details, but here we offer our suggestions for you to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For you to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand. And I thank you and I thank the Prosecutor for the suggestions. I don't think a 92 bis statement has the same value as viva voce statement. I don't think they would readily admit that. I don't think any lawyer that wants to be persuasive would agree that a statement called has the same value, persuasive value, as viva voce.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are not discussing about the value of those witnesses at this moment. I understand what you are saying but that's not subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I should restrain myself, Your Honour. Bring it on, Mr. Karnavas. If he has more witnesses like he's had in the last two weeks, bring them all on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think these are the comments we had for the live witnesses. Since your co-counsel is doing the 92 bis statements, I just offer some comments on those 92 bis witnesses for your consideration. And I believe that witness number 7, I don't think the information is specific enough in the 65 ter filings. If you want to introduce this witness as a 92 bis, we need more specific information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Number 8, number 8, we found that no additional information provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. If I may comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have the opportunity to comment on that when you are submitting your 92 bis filings at a later stage. Number 30, 3-0, we believe his testimony overlaps with number 24. The 65 ter filings did not describe activities or the orders of the witness. We don't know about his whereabouts. We need specific information on that. Number 37, it appears to us the testimony of this witness overlaps with 36, witness number 36. Number 45, you just offered to introduce this witness through 92 bis. We believe that his testimony is redundant in light of witness 46. There is no description of what the witness observed and heard on the night of 13th of July or of his trip to Pilica. Number 47, no additional information provided. Number 48, we believe it is repetitive of the two other witnesses, number 29 and number 30. Number 49, no additional information provided. Number 50, we believe that his testimony is redundant in light of the testimony of number 43. Number 52, we found that there is a lack of the additional information in his testimony. Number 53, we believe his testimony is redundant in light of 46. Number 55, we have serious doubts about admitting the statement of this witness through 92 bis because we believe that it tells us nothing, nothing described in that -- in the 65 ter filings. Number 56, we doubt about the relevancy of his testimony. Number 57, we believe his testimony is redundant in light of 43 and 54. Number 59, as I said that we believe that his testimony is cumulative with 65, 60, 40, 43, and 28. Number 60, redundant in light of 28. Number 62, redundant with 28. Number 68, cumulative in light of witness 22. Number 73, redundant in light of the witness 74. Well, I have to say that those suggestions were arrived by us on the 65 ter filings because we really did not see the statement of those witnesses. I believe that will be the next step. We offer our opinions and concerns at this stage with the sole purpose to help the Defence team to prepare the 92 bis statements. It will take some time for the Defence to submit their filings concerning of the 92 bis witnesses, and it will take some time for the Trial Chamber to read and study those statements. So, Mr. Karnavas, when could we have that 92 bis filings? You could just give us an approximate time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. We have several -- I don't know the exact number, I believe it's somewhere in the neighbourhood of 19 statements given for translation that are being -- we should have them any day now. And then some additional statements will be coming forward. So as soon as the first batch of the statements are translated, I was going to file the first portion. And then when we have -- and then while the other ones are being translated, at least the Trial Chamber would have the first ones. And then the ones that are about to come, hopefully shortly thereafter. So that way you have the statements themselves and you can decide whether you're going to disallow a witness or not. The 92 bis statements are short, they're very concise, two to three pages. They get to the heart. They answer all the questions that the Trial Chamber has requested, and though I don't want to make any excuses, one of the reasons some of the 92 bis statements are rather terse and maybe not as informative is because I was under the impression that you would have the statement itself and after reading it you would make that value judgement whether it was sufficient or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the 65 ter filings, Mr. Karnavas, since we are not, as I said before, quite satisfied with your filings, are you going to make a new one or make some supplement to these filings?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it by the nature of the question, it's an invitation for me to do so, and so I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. When are we going to have that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because the trial is going on at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I understand. I didn't have seven years for preparation, but I was hoping that I would buy some time since we have a free day next week. But I sense the Court has a certain urgency that it would like it as early as next week. So I'll try -- I'll try to get something done on these particular ones that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, just -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just briefly. I hope we can get proofing notes as well. We didn't get proofing notes from the last witness and it really didn't resemble the 65 ter summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So I hope we can continue to get that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that is a legitimate request.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I did indicate that he was going to be testifying pretty much as to the proofing notes earlier. I should also note that for instance -- since we're going to be at this route, with Jole Nikolic, I find out on the 11th-and-a-half hour that they haven't transcribed a statement, part of the statement, where he talks about the most critical aspect for five years. I don't stand up and complain, though I think I have every right to. It did complicate us, our situation, our proofing sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're doing the best as I can, Your Honour. As I recall I was getting proofing notes as I was walking into court on days. I didn't make a fuss because occasionally I would get a phone call being told what was on the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, even if it is true, tu quoque could not justify your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Touche.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I know that this Status Conference is devoted mainly to the Defence case for Mr. Blagojevic, but I ask Your Honour's leave to address you on two issues and I ask that this be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If there is nothing else, the hearing is adjourned.
